chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: The flat beat at Preservation Hall and why he fell out
summary: Danny says Preservation Hall wanted a straight static beat, and Allan Jaffe asked him to play straight instead of his lively figure-eight banjo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Woody Allen plays in the theme of George Lewis. It's a sad thing that... It's a lamentable thing, the way he plays. In fact, this guy... There's a whole cult behind George Lewis' band. That's one reason why I fell out of the Preservation Hall, because I played spirited banjo, the Figure-Eight stroke and...you know...

But them's people that play a straight, static beat -- BLUMP, BLUMP, BLUMP, BLUMP, BLUMP. A flat beat. That's what that band plays. Well, all them Europeans, it don't take you long (or the Japanese)...
Because it's the primitive beginning of playing. Almost... It doesn't even reach the Swing Era.
Yeah, you can duplicate it easily.
So that became... You can have the whining, the vibrato on a clarinet, and you got the slow, you know, Jim Robinson trombone...

And you got the trumpet with just a minimum of notes. But it's a sound within itself, with this (?). We use it for a youngster to form himself(?). Now, you give him a Duke Ellington record with Barney and Braud, like "Check and Double Check" or "Stompy Jones," where them people is really swinging -- well, they're in trouble.

So when I went to Preservation Hall, they told me, said, "Well, play it straight." That's what Jaffe told me. I said, "What do you mean 'play it straight'?" He said, "They just want you to play a straight beat." I said, "I don't play a straight beat. If feel it, (?) it needs a little rhythm in there." I ain't rushing tempos. I don't want to sell(?) myself, you dig? Because usually, when you want to play (?), you (?) you don't know to do that. Just play straight like you don't know what you're doing. That's what he's telling me. So I'm too advanced for the atmosphere.
It's too shocking. They want it placid and just play it with a bland face, you know.
Dig that, yeah. I hear what you mean.
them things in there -- "Oh, no." So they don't use a lot of musicians(?) there. [INAUDIBLE SENTENCE]
